title: task status-flow's manifest `fields` omits closedStatus and resolutions, which the command emits (QCLI-461 class)
description:
Found while landing QCLI-325 (review seq 8416) and reported then: task status-flow's advertised manifest `fields` is a CURATED SUBSET, not the complete key set -- the same under-declaration class QCLI-461 closed for task list, task view and search.

MEASURED. src/application/command-contract.ts declares fields [statuses, terminalStatuses, pausedStatus, pausedStatusConfigurable], while src/cli/commands/task/index.ts emits `closedStatus` and `resolutions` too whenever a closed status is configured. Nothing in-repo enforces status-flow's declared-versus-emitted set: QCLI-461's payload-subset-of-declared assertion runs over task view, task list and search only, and the adapter boundary comparison (test/contract/tracker/lore-adapter-boundary.test.ts) skips status-flow because ADAPTER_REQUIRED_MANIFEST_COMMANDS carries no `fields` key for it -- which is why bun run check passes with the two keys undeclared.

SAME CLASS AS QCLI-461 (which completed task list/view/search and deliberately left this surface alone). The fix is to declare the complete emitted key set for task status-flow, updating the manifest and its three mirrors together, and to extend the declared-versus-emitted assertion to cover it. Filed by the quest-cli worker at team-lead instruction -- the team-lead explicitly asked for this one; UNSTAMPED.

acceptanceCriteria.text: task status-flow's manifest `fields` contains every top-level key the command emits (closedStatus and resolutions included), updated in the manifest and its mirrors, and an assertion covers the emitted-subset-of-declared direction for it

finalSummary:
AC: task status-flow's manifest `fields` now declares the COMPLETE key set the command emits, in the manifest and its mirrors, and an assertion holds the emitted keys to it.

The emitted set, read from the PRODUCING SOURCE (src/cli/commands/task/index.ts): `statuses` and `terminalStatuses` always; `pausedStatus` and `pausedStatusConfigurable` when a paused status is configured; and `closedStatus` plus `resolutions` when a closed status is configured. A default workspace has both, so the complete possible set is those six -- and `closedStatus` and `resolutions` were always emitted while the manifest advertised a four-key curated subset, the same under-declaration QCLI-461 closed for task list, task view and search.

All the declaration sites move together: the manifest (src/application/command-contract.ts), its two mirrors (src/contract/tracker/index.ts, src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts), and the golden in test/contract/command-contract.test.ts, which the live-manifest test compares against.

The assertion lives in test/qcli325-paused-status-fixed.test.ts, beside the read it extends. It runs the real status-flow command on a workspace WITH a closed status configured -- the default -- asserts the emitted set CONTAINS `closedStatus` and `resolutions`, so the subset direction is not passing on silence, and then asserts every emitted key is declared. PROVED BOTH WAYS AND MEASURED: removing `closedStatus` from the declared list turns it red and names that key; removing `statuses` instead turns the subset assertion red with "emitted-but-undeclared: statuses". Both mutations were reverted; the tree is green.

RIDE-ALONG from QCLI-480's review, folded in here as instructed: the CHANGELOG sentence's "the platform-constraint fixtures" named no artifact in this repository (the string was unique to that line). It now names the public conformance fixture, src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts, which does carry the key. A CHANGELOG entry also records this change's manifest-fields extension.

Verified: bun run check exits 0 (1163 CLI tests, the mod suite 45 pass / 0 fail).
